claim: Transcoelomic spread of cancer cells across the peritoneal cavity occurs in most initially diagnosed ovarian cancer (OC) patients.
source: Transcoelomic spread of cancer cells across the peritoneal cavity occurs in most initially diagnosed ovarian cancer (OC) patients and accounts for most cancer-related death.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to established medical knowledge about ovarian cancer presentation patterns.

claim: Transcoelomic spread accounts for most cancer-related death in ovarian cancer.
source: Transcoelomic spread of cancer cells across the peritoneal cavity occurs in most initially diagnosed ovarian cancer (OC) patients and accounts for most cancer-related death.
evidence: This claim is supported by established medical knowledge about ovarian cancer mortality.

claim: IL20RA was identified as a key factor preventing the transcoelomic metastasis of OC through an in vivo genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen.
source: Here, through an in vivo genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen, we identified IL20RA, which decreased dramatically in OC patients during peritoneal metastasis, as a key factor preventing the transcoelomic metastasis of OC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the CRISPR screen described in the manuscript.

claim: IL20RA decreased dramatically in OC patients during peritoneal metastasis.
source: Here, through an in vivo genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen, we identified IL20RA, which decreased dramatically in OC patients during peritoneal metastasis, as a key factor preventing the transcoelomic metastasis of OC.
evidence: This claim is supported by patient sample data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Reconstitution of IL20RA in highly metastatic OC cells greatly suppresses the transcoelomic metastasis.
source: Reconstitution of IL20RA in highly metastatic OC cells greatly suppresses the transcoelomic metastasis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from mouse models shown in Figure 1.

claim: OC cells disseminating into the peritoneal cavity induce peritoneum mesothelial cells to express IL-20 and IL-24.
source: OC cells, when disseminate into the peritoneal cavity, greatly induce peritoneum mesothelial cells to express IL-20 and IL-24, which in turn activate the IL20RA downstream signaling in OC cells to produce mature IL-18, eventually resulting in the polarization of macrophages into the M1-like subtype to clear the cancer cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: IL-20 and IL-24 activate IL20RA downstream signaling in OC cells to produce mature IL-18.
source: OC cells, when disseminate into the peritoneal cavity, greatly induce peritoneum mesothelial cells to express IL-20 and IL-24, which in turn activate the IL20RA downstream signaling in OC cells to produce mature IL-18, eventually resulting in the polarization of macrophages into the M1-like subtype to clear the cancer cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: IL-18 produced by OC cells results in the polarization of macrophages into the M1-like subtype to clear the cancer cells.
source: OC cells, when disseminate into the peritoneal cavity, greatly induce peritoneum mesothelial cells to express IL-20 and IL-24, which in turn activate the IL20RA downstream signaling in OC cells to produce mature IL-18, eventually resulting in the polarization of macrophages into the M1-like subtype to clear the cancer cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3, 4, 5, 7, and 8.

claim: Ovarian cancer has the highest mortality among all gynecological malignancies.
source: Ovarian cancer (OC) has the highest mortality among all gynecological malignancies that seriously threatens women's health worldwide (Siegel et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Siegel et al., 2020.

claim: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) is the most common type of OC accounting for 90% of all cases.
source: Among OC, epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) is the most common type accounting for 90% of all cases (Farley et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Farley et al., 2008.

claim: EOC is classified by tumor cell histology as serous (52%), endometrioid (10%), mucinous (6%), clear cell (6%), and other rare subtypes.
source: EOC is classified by tumor cell histology as serous (52%), endometrioid (10%), mucinous (6%), clear cell (6%), and other rare subtypes.
evidence: This claim is supported by established medical classification knowledge.

claim: Approximately 70% of OC patients are already at metastatic stage (stages III and IV) at initial diagnosis.
source: Due to the lack of clear symptoms at the early stage, the spread of cancer cells across the peritoneal cavity occurs in most patients at the initial diagnosis, with approximately 70% of OC patients already at metastatic stage (stages III and IV) (Vaughan et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Vaughan et al., 2011.

claim: The 5-year survival rate is 20–40% for OC patients at advanced stages.
source: For OC patients with metastasized cancer cells, current therapies including chemotherapy and targeted therapies can only achieve very limited clinical outcome, with the 5-year survival rate of 20–40% for OC patients at advanced stages (Torre et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Torre et al., 2018.

claim: Transcoelomic metastasis of OC occurs most commonly compared to metastasis through blood vessels and lymphatic vessels.
source: Although OC cells can metastasize to other distant organs through blood vessels and lymphatic vessels, the transcoelomic metastasis of OC occurs most commonly, which includes multiple processes, such as detachment of tumor cells from primary sites, immune evasion of disseminated tumor cells in the peritoneal cavity, and colonization of tumor cells on the omentum and peritoneum (Tan et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tan et al., 2006.

claim: Transcoelomic metastasis includes detachment of tumor cells from primary sites, immune evasion of disseminated tumor cells in the peritoneal cavity, and colonization of tumor cells on the omentum and peritoneum.
source: Although OC cells can metastasize to other distant organs through blood vessels and lymphatic vessels, the transcoelomic metastasis of OC occurs most commonly, which includes multiple processes, such as detachment of tumor cells from primary sites, immune evasion of disseminated tumor cells in the peritoneal cavity, and colonization of tumor cells on the omentum and peritoneum (Tan et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tan et al., 2006.

claim: The peritoneal environment is constituted by lymphocytes, macrophages, natural killer (NK) cells, fibroblasts, mesothelial cells, as well as cytokines and chemokines secreted by these cells.
source: Disseminated OC cells have to survive in a peritoneal environment constituted by lymphocytes, macrophages, natural killer (NK) cells, fibroblasts, mesothelial cells, as well as cytokines and chemokines secreted by these cells for a successful transcoelomic metastasis (Ahmed and Stenvers, 2013; Worzfeld et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ahmed and Stenvers, 2013 and Worzfeld et al., 2017.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 knockout library has been successfully utilized to discover novel genes in the occurrence and development of diseases, especially in cancers.
source: To systematically identify key genes involved in the regulation of the peritoneal metastasis of OC, we performed genome-wide gene knockout screening in an orthotopic mouse model of OC by using CRISPR/Cas9 knockout library, which has been successfully utilized to discover novel genes in the occurrence and development of diseases, especially in cancers (Huang et al., 2019; Ng et al., 2020; Shalem et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Huang et al., 2019; Ng et al., 2020; Shalem et al., 2014.

claim: IL20RA is mainly expressed in epithelial cells.
source: IL20RA is mainly expressed in epithelial cells and forms the functional receptor, when heterodimerized with interleukin 20 receptor subunit beta (IL20RB), to bind immune cell-produced IL-20 subfamily of cytokines IL-19, IL-20, and IL-24, which have essential roles in regulating epithelial innate immunity and tissue repair (Rutz et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Rutz et al., 2014.

claim: IL20RA forms the functional receptor when heterodimerized with IL20RB.
source: IL20RA is mainly expressed in epithelial cells and forms the functional receptor, when heterodimerized with interleukin 20 receptor subunit beta (IL20RB), to bind immune cell-produced IL-20 subfamily of cytokines IL-19, IL-20, and IL-24, which have essential roles in regulating epithelial innate immunity and tissue repair (Rutz et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Rutz et al., 2014.

claim: IL20RA/IL20RB heterodimer binds immune cell-produced IL-20 subfamily of cytokines IL-19, IL-20, and IL-24.
source: IL20RA is mainly expressed in epithelial cells and forms the functional receptor, when heterodimerized with interleukin 20 receptor subunit beta (IL20RB), to bind immune cell-produced IL-20 subfamily of cytokines IL-19, IL-20, and IL-24, which have essential roles in regulating epithelial innate immunity and tissue repair (Rutz et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Rutz et al., 2014.

claim: IL-19, IL-20, and IL-24 have essential roles in regulating epithelial innate immunity and tissue repair.
source: IL20RA is mainly expressed in epithelial cells and forms the functional receptor, when heterodimerized with interleukin 20 receptor subunit beta (IL20RB), to bind immune cell-produced IL-20 subfamily of cytokines IL-19, IL-20, and IL-24, which have essential roles in regulating epithelial innate immunity and tissue repair (Rutz et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Rutz et al., 2014.

claim: IL20RA and IL20RB are detected in tumors of epithelial origin including breast cancer, non-small-cell lung cancer, and bladder cancer.
source: IL20RA and IL20RB are also detected in tumors of epithelial origin including breast cancer, non-small-cell lung cancer, and bladder cancer, while IL-20 subfamily of cytokines has been reported to have either tumor-promoting or tumor-suppressing roles depending on tumor types and the local immune environment (Gopalan et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2013; Pestka et al., 2004; Rutz et al., 2014; Whitaker et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Gopalan et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2013; Pestka et al., 2004; Rutz et al., 2014; Whitaker et al., 2012.

claim: IL-20 subfamily of cytokines has been reported to have either tumor-promoting or tumor-suppressing roles depending on tumor types and the local immune environment.
source: IL20RA and IL20RB are also detected in tumors of epithelial origin including breast cancer, non-small-cell lung cancer, and bladder cancer, while IL-20 subfamily of cytokines has been reported to have either tumor-promoting or tumor-suppressing roles depending on tumor types and the local immune environment (Gopalan et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2013; Pestka et al., 2004; Rutz et al., 2014; Whitaker et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Gopalan et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2013; Pestka et al., 2004; Rutz et al., 2014; Whitaker et al., 2012.

claim: SK-OV-3 cells were transduced with the human CRISPR knockout library (GeCKO v2.0) containing sgRNAs specifically against 19,050 protein-encoding genes and 1864 miRNA genes and 1000 non-targeting control sgRNAs.
source: Prior to the inoculation of these cells into the mouse ovaries, SK-OV-3 cells were transduced with the human CRISPR knockout library (GeCKO v2.0) made by Feng Zhang et al., which contains sgRNAs specifically against 19,050 protein-encoding genes and 1864 miRNA genes and 1000 non-targeting control sgRNAs (Shalem et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Shalem et al., 2014 and describes the experimental method.

claim: After three runs of in vivo screening, two high-ranked genes were identified: IL20RA and TEX14.
source: By using the criteria of the number of enriched sgRNAs targeting each gene ≥3, p-value<0.05 and the normalized enrichment score (NES) <−1.2, we got two high-ranked genes, namely IL20RA and TEX14 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: All six sgRNAs targeting IL20RA in GeCKO library were enriched with high NES.
source: Given all the six sgRNAs targeting IL20RA in GeCKO library were enriched with high NES, we chose IL20RA for further investigation on its function in the transcoelomic metastasis of OC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the CRISPR screen.

claim: Silencing IL20RA in SK-OV-3 cells greatly promoted the transcoelomic metastasis of OC and the formation of ascites in the orthotopic mouse OC model.
source: In the SK-OV-3 orthotopic mouse OC model, silencing IL20RA greatly promoted the transcoelomic metastasis of OC and the formation of ascites (Figure 1E, F)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: Reconstitution of IL20RA in ID8 cells dramatically reduced the volumes of ascites and the numbers of metastatic nodules in diaphragm, peritoneum, and mesentery in the ID8 syngeneic mouse OC model.
source: while in ID8 syngeneic mouse OC model, reconstitution of IL20RA in ID8 cells dramatically reduced the volumes of ascites and the numbers of metastatic nodules in diaphragm, peritoneum, and mesentery (Figure 1G, H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G and H.

claim: IL20RA-reconstituted ID8 cells formed much less metastases on the diaphragm, peritoneum, and mesentery and resulted in much less ascites when directly injected into the peritoneal cavity of C57BL/6 mice.
source: To further investigate whether IL20RA suppresses transcoelomic metastasis of OC at the later stage when OC cells have disseminated into the peritoneal cavity, we directly injected ID8 cells into the peritoneal cavity of C57BL/6 mice. We were still able to observe that IL20RA-reconstituted ID8 cells formed much less metastases on the diaphragm, peritoneum, and mesentery and resulted in much less ascites as well (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, D.

claim: Western blot analysis shows a dramatic decrease of IL20RA in the transcoelomic spread cancer samples when compared with those from the primary sites in 20 serous OC patients.
source: Analysis of IL20RA protein by western blot shows a dramatic decrease of IL20RA in the transcoelomic spread cancer samples when compared with those from the primary sites (Figure 2A, B)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: qRT-PCR analysis confirmed the dramatic decrease of IL20RA mRNA in metastatic samples compared to primary sites.
source: which is confirmed by the quantitative reverse-transcriptase-PCR (qRT-PCR) analysis of IL20RA mRNA (Figure 2C, D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis shows much lower level of IL20RA in metastatic cancer cells than that in the cancer cells at the primary sites.
source: Immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis also shows the much lower level of IL20RA in metastatic cancer cells than that in the cancer cells at the primary sites (Figure 2E, F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E and F.

claim: High level of IL20RA significantly correlates with the better overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) of serous OC patients.
source: High level of IL20RA significantly correlates with the better overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) of serous OC patients (Figure 2G)
evidence: This claim is supported by survival analysis data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: IL20RA expression is positively correlated with the clinical outcome of patients with bladder carcinoma, uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma, rectum adenocarcinoma, and gastric cancer.
source: Besides, IL20RA expression is also positively correlated with the clinical outcome of patients in patients of bladder carcinoma, uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma, rectum adenocarcinoma, and gastric cancer (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by survival analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: IL20RB expression shows no significant difference between primary and metastatic OC specimen.
source: By contrast, as a heterodimerization partner for IL20RA, IL20RB expression shows no significant difference between primary and metastatic OC specimen (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: IL20RB negatively correlates with the OS and PFS of OC patients.
source: and negatively correlates with the OS and PFS of OC patients (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C)
evidence: This claim is supported by survival analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: IL20RA does not regulate the proliferation and migration of OC cells.
source: To get insights into the mechanisms of IL20RA-mediated inhibition on OC metastasis, we firstly excluded the possibility that IL20RA might regulate the proliferation and migration of OC cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: Reconstitution of IL20RA does not change the total proportion of macrophages (CD11b+ F4/80+) among leukocytes (CD45+) in ascites.
source: Compared with control ID8 cells with very low level of endogenous IL20RA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), reconstitution of IL20RA does not change the total proportion of macrophages (CD11b+ F4/80+) among leukocytes (CD45+).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from flow cytometry analysis.

claim: Reconstitution of IL20RA significantly increases the proportion of M1-like (MHCII+ CD206-) macrophages in the malignant ascites.
source: However, we observed a significant increase in the proportion of M1-like (MHCII+ CD206-) macrophages and a dramatic decrease of M2-like (MHCII- CD206+) macrophages in the malignant ascites caused by IL20RA-reconstituted ID8 cells (Figure 3A, B)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Reconstitution of IL20RA dramatically decreases M2-like (MHCII- CD206+) macrophages in the malignant ascites.
source: However, we observed a significant increase in the proportion of M1-like (MHCII+ CD206-) macrophages and a dramatic decrease of M2-like (MHCII- CD206+) macrophages in the malignant ascites caused by IL20RA-reconstituted ID8 cells (Figure 3A, B)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: IL20RA-mediated changes in macrophage polarization were confirmed by dramatically increased M1-like marker genes and decreased M2-like markers.
source: which were further confirmed by dramatically increased M1-like marker genes and decreased M2-like markers (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Neither the ratios of T lymphocytes (CD45+ CD3+) and their subtypes (CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes) nor that of B lymphocytes (CD45+ B220+) showed significant change upon the reconstitution of IL20RA.
source: We also found that neither the ratios of T lymphocytes (CD45+ CD3+) and their subtypes (i.e., CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes) nor that of B lymphocytes (CD45+ B220+) showed significant change upon the reconstitution of IL20RA (Figure 3D, E)
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: The population of M1-like (MHCII+) macrophages is significantly decreased and M2-like (CD206+) macrophages is significantly increased upon silencing IL20RA in SK-OV-3 cells in NOD-SCID mice.
source: FACS results show that the population of M1-like (MHCII+) macrophages is significantly decreased and M2-like (CD206+) macrophages is significantly increased upon silencing IL20RA (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: IL20RA in OC cells is able to regulate the polarization of peritoneal macrophages, instead of T lymphocytes and B lymphocytes, to prevent the transcoelomic spreading of OC cells into the peritoneal cavity.
source: Collectively, these data demonstrate that IL20RA in OC cells is able to regulate the polarization of peritoneal macrophages, instead of T lymphocytes and B lymphocytes, to prevent the transcoelomic spreading of OC cells into the peritoneal cavity.
evidence: This claim is supported by the collective experimental data from Figures 3 and related experiments.

claim: CM from IL-20-stimulated IL20RA-reconstituted ID8 cells significantly stimulates the expression of M1-like markers while decreases the expression of M2-like markers in RAW 264.7 cells.
source: CM from IL-20-stimulated IL20RA-reconstituted ID8 cells (hereafter referred to as 'CMIL20RA IL-20 (+)) significantly stimulates the expression of M1-like markers while decreases the expression of M2-like markers in RAW 264.7 cells when compared with CM from IL-20-stimulated empty vector-transfected ID8 control cells (referred to as CMVec IL-20 (+)) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: CMIL20RA IL-20 (+) dramatically induces the expression of M1-like markers and decreases the M2-like markers in BMDM.
source: Consistently, CMIL20RA IL-20 (+) dramatically induces the expression of M1-like markers and decreases the M2-like markers in BMDM (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: CM from IL-20-stimulated, IL20RA-silenced SK-OV-3 cells significantly increases the expression of M2-like markers and decreases the expression of M1-like markers in THP-1-derived macrophages.
source: In human macrophages differentiated from THP-1 monocytes by phorbol-12-myristate-13-acetate (PMA) treatment (Figure 4F, G), CM from IL-20-stimulated, IL20RA-silenced SK-OV-3 cells significantly increases the expression of M2-like markers and decreases the expression of M1-like markers when compared with CM from IL-20-stimulated control shRNA (shCtrl)-transfected SK-OV-3 cells (Figure 4H).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: IL20RA-mediated macrophage polarization needs the prior stimulation of IL-20.
source: Besides, the polarization of macrophages is not changed under the stimulation of CM from unstimulated IL20RA-reconstituted or IL20RA-silenced OC cells, indicating that IL20RA-mediated macrophage polarization needs the prior stimulation of the IL-20 (Figure 4B, E, H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B, E, H.

claim: IL-20 and IL-24 do not directly regulate the polarization of macrophages.
source: We also excluded the possibility that IL-20 and IL-24 directly regulated the polarization of macrophages since it did not affect the expression of both the M1- and M2-like markers in RAW 264.7 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F, G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F, G.

claim: CMIL20RA IL-20 (+)-educated BMDM significantly reduces the volume of malignant ascites when co-injected with ID8 cells into the peritoneal cavity of C57BL/6 mice.
source: CMIL20RA IL-20 (+)-educated BMDM significantly reduces the volume of malignant ascites (Figure 5B, C)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claim: CMIL20RA IL-20 (+)-educated BMDM dramatically inhibits the formation of metastatic nodules in peritoneal cavity when co-injected with ID8 cells.
source: and dramatically inhibits the formation of metastatic nodules in peritoneal cavity (Figure 5D, E)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: In peritoneal macrophage-depleted mice, reconstitution of IL20RA in ID8 cells can no longer reduce the volume of malignant ascites and inhibit the peritoneal metastasis of OC.
source: In addition, in peritoneal macrophage-depleted mice, reconstitution of IL20RA in ID8 cells can no longer reduce the volume of malignant ascites and inhibit the peritoneal metastasis of OC, indicating that IL20RA-mediated education of macrophages plays an essential role to suppress the transcoelomic metastasis of OC (Figure 5F–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F–J.

claim: IL20RA-mediated education of macrophages plays an essential role to suppress the transcoelomic metastasis of OC.
source: In addition, in peritoneal macrophage-depleted mice, reconstitution of IL20RA in ID8 cells can no longer reduce the volume of malignant ascites and inhibit the peritoneal metastasis of OC, indicating that IL20RA-mediated education of macrophages plays an essential role to suppress the transcoelomic metastasis of OC (Figure 5F–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F–J and logical inference from the macrophage depletion experiment.

claim: A dramatic increase of Il20 and Il24 from the abdominal wall occurs upon the injection of OC cells into the peritoneal cavity.
source: A dramatic increase of Il20 and Il24 from the abdominal wall occurs upon the injection of OC cells into the peritoneal cavity (Figure 6A)
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: There is no induction of IL20RA ligands in the intestine, ovary, and peritoneal macrophages upon injection of OC cells into the peritoneal cavity.
source: while there is no induction of these ligands in the intestine, ovary, and peritoneal macrophages (CD11b+ F4/80+) (Figure 6A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: Reconstitution of IL20RA in ID8 cells does not induce IL20RA ligands in themselves.
source: In addition, reconstitution of IL20RA in ID8 cells does not induce these ligands in themselves (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The amounts of IL-20 and IL-24 in peritoneal flushing fluid are significantly increased upon the injection of OC cells into the peritoneal cavity.
source: The amounts of IL-20 and IL-24 in peritoneal flushing fluid are significantly increased upon the injection of OC cells into the peritoneal cavity (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Co-culture of abdominal wall with ID8 cells in vitro resulted in boosted expression of Il20 and Il24.
source: To further confirm, we isolated abdominal wall and co-cultured with ID8 cells in vitro and a boosted expression of Il20 and Il24 was observed (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: IL-20 and IL-24 are originated from mesothelial cells in the abdominal walls from mice bearing peritoneal-disseminated OC cells.
source: Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and IHC staining of the abdominal walls from mice bearing peritoneal-disseminated OC cells show that IL-20 and IL-24 are originated from mesothelial cells (Figure 6F, G), which are further confirmed by immunofluorescent (IF) staining (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC and IF data shown in Figure 6F, G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: IL-20/IL20RA-mediated signaling greatly increases the expression of Oas1a, Oas1g, and Il18 involved in OAS-RNase L-mediated NOD-like receptor (NLR) signaling pathway.
source: In particular, IL-20/IL20RA-mediated signaling greatly increases the expression of several genes, that is, 2'−5'-oligoadenylate synthetase (Oas1a and Oas1g) and Il18, involved in OAS-RNase L-mediated NOD-like receptor (NLR) signaling pathway (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B, C)
evidence: This claim is supported by transcriptome data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: OAS-RNase L-mediated NLR signaling pathway regulates inflammasome signaling to activate Caspase-1 and hence the production of functional inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18 by cleavage during viral infections.
source: which regulates inflammasome signaling to activate Caspase-1 and hence the production of functional inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18 by cleavage during viral infections (Banerjee, 2016; Chakrabarti et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Banerjee, 2016 and Chakrabarti et al., 2015.

claim: IL-20/IL20RA triggers the phosphorylation of STAT3 and results in increased OAS1A, activated Caspase-1 and IL-18 by cleavage in ID8 cells.
source: Western blot analysis shows that IL-20/IL20RA triggers the phosphorylation of STAT3 and results in increased OAS1A, activated Caspase-1 and IL-18 by cleavage (Figure 7C)
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: IL-20 stimulation activates STAT3 and increases OAS1, Caspase-1, and IL-18 in human SK-OV-3 cells.
source: which also occurs in human SK-OV-3 cells when stimulated by IL-20 (Figure 7D, E).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot and ELISA data shown in Figure 7D and E.

claim: A STAT3-binding site exists on the promoter of Oas1a gene.
source: We further identify a STAT3-binding site on the promoter of Oas1a gene by chromatin immunoprecipitation and qPCR (ChIP-qPCR) (Figure 7F, G)
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7F and G.

claim: IL-20/IL20RA induces Oas1a and Il18 through downstream STAT3.
source: confirming that IL-20/IL20RA induces Oas1a and Il18 through downstream STAT3.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data and logical inference from the STAT3 binding site identification.

claim: The levels of phosphorylated STAT3, OAS1, and IL-18 are significantly lower in metastatic lesions than those in primary sites in human OC tissues.
source: Consistently, IHC staining of human OC tissues shows that the levels of phosphorylated STAT3, OAS1, and IL-18 are significantly lower in metastatic lesions than those in primary sites (Figure 7H, I).
evidence: This claim is supported by IHC data shown in Figure 7H and I.

claim: IL20RA positively correlates with both OAS1 and IL18 in a cohort of 530 serous OC patients from TCGA database.
source: In addition, transcriptome analysis on a cohort of 530 serous OC patients from TCGA database shows the positive correlation of IL20RA with both OAS1 and IL18 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D.

claim: IL-18 treatment greatly increases expression of M1-like markers and significantly decreases M2-like markers in RAW 264.7 cells.
source: To get insights into the role of IL-18 in macrophage polarization, RAW 264.7 cells were treated with IL-18, which resulted in greatly increased expression of M1-like markers and significantly decreased M2-like markers (Figure 7J).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 7J.

claim: CMIL20RA IL-20 (+)-induced polarization of RAW 264.7 cells to M1-like phenotypes can be dramatically blocked by IL-18 neutralization antibody.
source: CMIL20RA IL-20 (+)-induced polarization of RAW 264.7 cells to M1-like phenotypes can be dramatically blocked by IL-18 neutralization antibody (Figure 7K).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 7K.

claim: Silencing IL-18 abolishes the effects of reconstituted IL20RA in the inhibition of the malignant ascites formation and the peritoneal dissemination of OC cells.
source: Silencing IL-18 abolishes the effects of reconstituted IL20RA in the inhibition of the malignant ascites formation and the peritoneal dissemination of OC cells (Figure 8D–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8D–G.

claim: IL-20/IL20RA-induced polarization of peritoneal macrophages to M1-like phenotypes is disappeared upon the silencing of IL-18.
source: In addition, IL-20/IL20RA-induced polarization of peritoneal macrophages to M1-like phenotypes is also disappeared upon the silenced of IL-18 (Figure 8H).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8H.

claim: IL-18 is the essential factor downstream IL-20/IL20RA signaling to regulate the polarization of macrophages and suppress the OC dissemination.
source: These data suggest that IL-18 is the essential factor downstream IL-20/IL20RA signaling to regulate the polarization of macrophages and suppress the OC dissemination.
evidence: This claim is supported by the collective experimental data from IL-18 knockdown experiments and logical inference.

claim: Silencing IL20RB blocks the activation of the STAT3/NLR signaling in IL20RA-reconstituted ID8 cells.
source: Western blot analysis and qRT-PCR analysis show that silencing IL20RB blocks the activation of the STAT3/NLR signaling in IL20RA-reconstituted ID8 cells and hence the polarization of macrophages educated by ID8 cells (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: Silencing IL20RB in IL20RA-reconstituted ID8 cells dramatically abolishes the suppressive roles of IL20RA in the formation of malignant ascites and the peritoneal dissemination of OC cells.
source: In ID8 cell-grafted murine model of OC, silencing IL20RB in IL20RA-reconstituted ID8 cells dramatically abolishes the suppressive roles of IL20RA in the formation of malignant ascites and the peritoneal dissemination of OC cells, indicating that IL20RA signaling-inhibited OC dissemination needs the functional IL20RA/IL20RB heterodimer receptor (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1D–G.

claim: IL20RA signaling-inhibited OC dissemination needs the functional IL20RA/IL20RB heterodimer receptor.
source: In ID8 cell-grafted murine model of OC, silencing IL20RB in IL20RA-reconstituted ID8 cells dramatically abolishes the suppressive roles of IL20RA in the formation of malignant ascites and the peritoneal dissemination of OC cells, indicating that IL20RA signaling-inhibited OC dissemination needs the functional IL20RA/IL20RB heterodimer receptor (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1D–G and logical inference.

claim: Intraperitoneal injection of SK-OV-3 cells induces the increased expression of Il20 and Il24 from the abdominal wall of C57BL/6 mice.
source: Intraperitoneal injection of SK-OV-3 cells induces the increased expression of Il20 and Il24 from the abdominal wall of C57BL/6 mice (Figure 8—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Murine IL-20 subfamily cytokines are able to cross-react with human receptors.
source: Besides, a previous study has showed that murine IL-20 subfamily cytokines were also able to cross-react with human receptors (Kolumam et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kolumam et al., 2017.

claim: Human IL-18 significantly stimulates the expression of M1-like markers while inhibits the expression of M2-like markers in RAW 264.7 cells.
source: In addition, human IL-18 also significantly stimulates the expression of M1-like markers while inhibits the expression of M2-like markers in RAW 264.7 cells (Figure 8—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Intraperitoneal injection of IL-18 dramatically reduces the ascites formation and the numbers of metastatic nodules in diaphragm, peritoneum, and mesentery in mice bearing orthotopically transplanted ID8 xenografts.
source: It shows that intraperitoneal injection of IL-18 dramatically reduces the ascites formation and the numbers of metastatic nodules in diaphragm, peritoneum, and mesentery (Figure 9B–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9B–E.

claim: Direct administration of IL-18 significantly increases the proportion of M1-like (MHCII+ CD206-) macrophages and decreases M2-like (MHCII- CD206+) macrophages in the malignant ascites.
source: Furthermore, direct administration of IL-18 significantly increases the proportion of M1-like (MHCII+ CD206-) macrophages and decreases M2-like (MHCII- CD206+) macrophages in the malignant ascites (Figure 9F).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 9F.

claim: Highly metastatic OC cells block the IL-20/IL20RA/IL-18 pathway by decreasing IL20RA expression.
source: Highly metastatic OC cells always block this pathway by decreasing IL20RA expression, suggesting that reactivation of its downstream signaling, such as the application of IL-18, could be a useful strategy for the therapy of OC at advanced stages.
evidence: This claim is supported by the collective experimental data and logical inference from the study.

claim: Reactivation of IL20RA downstream signaling, such as the application of IL-18, could be a useful strategy for the therapy of OC at advanced stages.
source: Highly metastatic OC cells always block this pathway by decreasing IL20RA expression, suggesting that reactivation of its downstream signaling, such as the application of IL-18, could be a useful strategy for the therapy of OC at advanced stages.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing IL-18 efficacy and represents a speculative therapeutic suggestion.

claim: Transcoelomic metastasis occurs in about 70% of OC patients and many other types of cancers, such as pancreatic cancer, gastric cancer, endometrial cancer, and colon cancer.
source: The common metastasis mode of OC is transcoelomic metastasis, in which the cancer cells disseminate into the peritoneal cavity and colonize on the peritoneum and abdominal organs. Transcoelomic metastasis occurs in about 70% of OC patients and many other types of cancers, such as pancreatic cancer, gastric cancer, endometrial cancer, and colon cancer (Mikuła-Pietrasik et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Mikuła-Pietrasik et al., 2018.

claim: Patients with transcoelomic metastasis are diagnosed at stages III and IV, which means high mortality and poor prognosis.
source: Patients with transcoelomic metastasis are diagnosed at stages III and IV, which means high mortality and poor prognosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by established medical knowledge about cancer staging.

claim: IL-20/IL20RA-mediated crosstalk between cancer cells and peritoneum mesothelial cells eventually promotes the generation of M1-like inflammatory macrophages to prevent peritoneal dissemination of OC cells.
source: In the present study, we discovered a novel IL-20/IL20RA-mediated crosstalk between disseminated OC cells and peritoneum mesothelial cells that eventually promotes the generation of M1-like inflammatory macrophages to prevent peritoneal dissemination of OC cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by the collective experimental data from the study.

claim: This peritoneal-specific immune modulation mechanism may also happen in other types of cancers that can disseminate into the peritoneal cavity, such as gastric cancer, endometrial carcinoma, colon cancer, and bladder carcinoma.
source: This peritoneal-specific immune modulation mechanism may also happen in other types of cancers that can disseminate into the peritoneal cavity, such as gastric cancer, endometrial carcinoma, colon cancer, and bladder carcinoma, in which the high expression of IL20RA also correlates with a better clinical outcome of patients (Figure 2—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by survival analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and represents a speculative extension of findings.

claim: Immune cell-produced IL-20 subfamily cytokines and their receptors mainly expressed in epithelial cells facilitate the crosstalk between leukocytes and epithelial cells.
source: Immune cell-produced IL-20 subfamily cytokines and their receptors mainly expressed in epithelial cells facilitate the crosstalk between leukocytes and epithelial cells, which has essential functions in epithelial innate immunity for the host defense and tissue repair at epithelial surfaces.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about IL-20 subfamily cytokines.

claim: IL-20 and IL-26 promote proliferation and migration of bladder cancer, breast cancer, and gastric cancer cells.
source: IL-20 and IL-26 were discovered to promote proliferation and migration of bladder cancer, breast cancer, and gastric cancer cells, while IL-24 was found to inhibit the proliferation and metastasis of melanoma, prostate cancer, and OC (Fisher et al., 2007; Gopalan et al., 2007; Hsu et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2013; Pradhan et al., 2018; You et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fisher et al., 2007; Gopalan et al., 2007; Hsu et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2013; Pradhan et al., 2018; You et al., 2013.

claim: IL-24 inhibits the proliferation and metastasis of melanoma, prostate cancer, and OC.
source: IL-20 and IL-26 were discovered to promote proliferation and migration of bladder cancer, breast cancer, and gastric cancer cells, while IL-24 was found to inhibit the proliferation and metastasis of melanoma, prostate cancer, and OC (Fisher et al., 2007; Gopalan et al., 2007; Hsu et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2013; Pradhan et al., 2018; You et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fisher et al., 2007; Gopalan et al., 2007; Hsu et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2013; Pradhan et al., 2018; You et al., 2013.

claim: STAT3 can switch its roles from tumor-promoting at early stages to tumor-suppressing in the invasion process.
source: Although IL-20 subfamily cytokines have been extensively reported to activate STAT3 to exhibit oncogenic effects, STAT3 has also been shown to be able to switch its roles from tumor-promoting at early stages to tumor-suppressing in the invasion process (Musteanu et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Musteanu et al., 2010.

claim: Cancer cell-mediated conversion of omentum stromal cells, including adipocytes, fibroblasts, macrophages, and mesenchymal stem cells, to cancer-associated stromal cells is of vital importance for the metastatic growth of OC cells on omentum.
source: For OC metastasized to omentum, cancer cell-mediated conversion of omentum stromal cells, including adipocytes, fibroblasts, macrophages, and mesenchymal stem cells, to cancer-associated stromal cells is of vital importance for the metastatic growth of OC cells on omentum (Motohara et al., 2019; Thibault et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Motohara et al., 2019 and Thibault et al., 2014.

claim: Mesothelial cells form the first line of defense against microbial pathogens through the expression of retinoic acid-inducible gene-I-like (RIG-I–like) receptors, Toll-like receptors, and C-type lectin-like receptors.
source: The abdominal cavity is lined with a layer of mesothelial cells that form the first line of defense against microbial pathogens through the expression of retinoic acid-inducible gene-I-like (RIG-I–like) receptors, Toll-like receptors, and C-type lectin-like receptors (Colmont et al., 2011; Kato et al., 2004; Park et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Colmont et al., 2011; Kato et al., 2004; Park et al., 2007.

claim: Mesothelial cells can secret cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors to regulate the inflammatory responses in peritoneal cavity.
source: Besides, mesothelial cells can secret cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors to regulate the inflammatory responses in peritoneal cavity (Isaza-Restrepo et al., 2018; Yao et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Isaza-Restrepo et al., 2018 and Yao et al., 2004.

claim: It is more difficult for OC cells to attach to mesothelial cells compared with the extracellular matrix and the fibroblasts.
source: It is more difficult for OC cells to attach to mesothelial cells compared with the extracellular matrix and the fibroblasts (Agarwal et al., 2019; Kenny et al., 2007; Niedbala et al., 1985).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Agarwal et al., 2019; Kenny et al., 2007; Niedbala et al., 1985.

claim: OC cells can destroy the mesothelial cell layer by promoting the mesothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (MMT) of mesothelial cells and hence the loss of cell-cell adherence.
source: During the metastatic growth, OC cells can destroy the mesothelial cell layer by promoting the mesothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (MMT) of mesothelial cells and hence the loss of cell-cell adherence (Iwanicki et al., 2011; Kenny et al., 2011; Sandoval et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Iwanicki et al., 2011; Kenny et al., 2011; Sandoval et al., 2013.

claim: Mesothelial cells can actively respond to OC cells invaded into the peritoneal cavity by secreting IL-20 and IL-24 to communicate with OC cells.
source: Here, we revealed, for the first time, that mesothelial cells can actively respond to OC cells invaded into the peritoneal cavity by secreting IL-20 and IL-24 to communicate with OC cells, consequently resulting in a further crosstalk between OC cells and macrophages for the formation of an antitumor microenvironment.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the study and represents a novel finding.

claim: Successfully metastasized OC cells overcome the mesothelial-initiated defense mechanism through the downregulation of IL-20/IL-24 receptor IL20RA.
source: This mesothelial-initiated defense mechanism is oftentimes overcome by successfully metastasized OC cells through the downregulation of IL-20/IL-24 receptor IL20RA (Figure 2A–F) to shut down the communication between OC and mesothelial cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A–F and logical inference.

claim: In OC patients the majority of cell types in ascites are lymphocytes (37%) and macrophages (32%).
source: It has been reported that in OC patients the majority of cell types in ascites are lymphocytes (37%) and macrophages (32%), contributing to the progression and metastasis of OC (Kipps et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kipps et al., 2013.

claim: The ratio of M1/M2-subtype macrophages has predictive value for the prognosis of OC patients, with a higher M1/M2-subtype ratio being associated with a better prognosis.
source: The ratio of M1/M2-subtype macrophages has predictive value for the prognosis of OC patients, with a higher M1/M2-subtype ratio being associated with a better prognosis, while a higher CD163+ (M2-subtype)/CD68+ (total macrophages) ratio with a poor prognosis (Reinartz et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Reinartz et al., 2014 and Zhang et al., 2014.

claim: A higher CD163+ (M2-subtype)/CD68+ (total macrophages) ratio is associated with a poor prognosis in OC patients.
source: The ratio of M1/M2-subtype macrophages has predictive value for the prognosis of OC patients, with a higher M1/M2-subtype ratio being associated with a better prognosis, while a higher CD163+ (M2-subtype)/CD68+ (total macrophages) ratio with a poor prognosis (Reinartz et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Reinartz et al., 2014 and Zhang et al., 2014.

claim: Host-produced histidine-rich glycoprotein (HRG) could inhibit the growth and metastasis of tumors via re-polarizing the macrophages from M2-subtype to M1-subtype.
source: It has reported that host-produced histidine-rich glycoprotein (HRG) could inhibit the growth and metastasis of tumors via re-polarizing the macrophages from M2-subtype to M1-subtype (Rolny et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Rolny et al., 2011.

claim: Nanoparticles encapsulating miR-125b could specifically re-polarize the peritoneal macrophages to M1-subtype, thereby improving the efficacy of paclitaxel in OC.
source: Nanoparticles encapsulating miR-125b could specifically re-polarize the peritoneal macrophages to M1-subtype, thereby improving the efficacy of paclitaxel in OC (Parayath et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Parayath et al., 2019.

claim: IL-18 is an immunoregulatory cytokine with anti-cancer effect in many types of cancers.
source: IL-18 is an immunoregulatory cytokine with anti-cancer effect in many types of cancers (Coughlin et al., 1998; Nishio et al., 2008; Salcedo et al., 2010; Zaki et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Coughlin et al., 1998; Nishio et al., 2008; Salcedo et al., 2010; Zaki et al., 2010.

claim: The normal ovarian and colon epithelia have the capacity to process and release active IL-18.
source: The normal ovarian and colon epithelia have the capacity to process and release active IL-18, thereby supporting a local antitumor immune microenvironment.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about IL-18 processing in normal epithelia.

claim: During malignant transformation, ovarian and colon cancer cells lose the ability to process IL-18 as a result of defective Caspase-1 activation.
source: However, during the malignant transformation, the ovarian and colon cancer cells lose the ability to process IL-18 as a result of the defective Caspase-1 activation (Feng et al., 2005; Wang et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Feng et al., 2005 and Wang et al., 2002.

claim: OC cells express more pro-IL-18 but poorly produce mature-IL-18.
source: Thus, OC cells express more pro-IL-18 but poorly produce mature-IL-18.
evidence: This claim is supported by logical inference from the defective Caspase-1 activation in cancer cells.

claim: Elevated IL-18 was reported in the ascites and sera of OC patients in a 23 kDa pre-form, whereas the 18 kDa mature and active form was undetectable.
source: Elevated IL-18 was reported in the ascites and sera of OC patients in a 23 kDa pre-form, whereas the 18 kDa mature and active form was undetectable (Orengo et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Orengo et al., 2011.

claim: Reconstitution of IL20RA in highly metastatic OC cells can reactivate the production of mature IL-18 via IL-20/IL20RA-OAS1/RNase L-NLR axis.
source: Here, we show that reconstitution of IL20RA in highly metastatic OC cells can reactivate the production of mature IL-18 via IL-20/IL20RA-OAS1/RNase L-NLR axis, suggesting the silence of IL20RA to be a possible reason for the loss of mature IL-18 in OC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the study and represents a mechanistic finding.

claim: The silence of IL20RA is a possible reason for the loss of mature IL-18 in OC.
source: Here, we show that reconstitution of IL20RA in highly metastatic OC cells can reactivate the production of mature IL-18 via IL-20/IL20RA-OAS1/RNase L-NLR axis, suggesting the silence of IL20RA to be a possible reason for the loss of mature IL-18 in OC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and represents a speculative inference.

claim: IL-18 has been shown to exert antitumor activity through the activation of T cell.
source: IL-18 has been shown to exert antitumor activity through the activation of T cell (Fabbi et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Fabbi et al., 2015.

claim: Several clinical trials testing the antitumor efficacy of IL-18 have been conducted in lymphomas and melanoma.
source: Several clinical trials testing the antitumor efficacy of IL-18 have been conducted in lymphomas and melanoma (Robertson et al., 2013; Robertson et al., 2006; Tarhini et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Robertson et al., 2013; Robertson et al., 2006; Tarhini et al., 2009.

claim: The administration of recombinant IL-18 significantly suppresses the metastasis of IL20RA-deficient OC cells.
source: Our study shows that the administration of recombinant IL-18 significantly suppresses the metastasis of IL20RA-deficient OC cells, suggesting the great value of IL-18 in the therapy of OC at advanced stages.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the IL-18 treatment experiments.

claim: ID8 cells were isolated from peritoneal ascites of ID8-injected C57BL/6 mice with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC)-like characteristics.
source: and reconstituted IL20RA in highly metastatic murine epithelial OC cell ID8, which was isolated from peritoneal ascites of ID8-injected C57BL/6 mice as described by Ward and colleagues (Ward et al., 2013) with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC)-like characteristics (Diaz Osterman et al., 2019)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ward et al., 2013 and Diaz Osterman et al., 2019.
